title: Explain KV caching in three sentences.

messages.content: Explain KV caching in three sentences.

Kernel Virtual Memory (KV caching) is a technique used by operating systems to improve the performance of applications by storing frequently accessed data in a virtual memory space, reducing the need to access physical memory. This allows the kernel to process requests more efficiently, as it can access data directly in the virtual memory space without having to translate it to physical memory. By minimizing the number of times the application needs to access physical memory, KV caching can improve overall system performance and responsiveness.
